agentCan: Implement the authorization-code flow (PKCE and Device Grant also supported) with refresh handling
Prepare the App Hub submission packet (marketing materials, demo accounts, listing assets)
Implement Service App org-authorization flows and token retrieval if you ship that flavor

approval.trigger: Integrations: no Cisco review before real users can connect; users in your org can add an unlisted app, and the docs describe no approval gate for the integration itself. Webex App Hub listing is optional and discoverability-only: a two-phase review (public-facing marketing materials, then functionality/usability testing with demo accounts across major OS/device platforms) with change requests by email. Service Apps are different: each customer org's Full Admin must authorize the app in Control Hub, and for non-affiliated orgs you must first submit the Service App to App Hub, which 'initiates a manual review of your Service App with the App Hub team'.
approval.wait: No stated timeline for App Hub review ('depending on how quickly the proposed changes are addressed, the review process can move very quickly'); a Cisco developer blog (not documentation) says embedded-app review generally takes around 2-3 weeks, do not plan on that figure

blockers.detail: Each Webex user account may create at most 20 integrations. Developer and test accounts burn this quota quickly, and the cap is on the account, not per org.
blockers.howToClear: Consolidate test integrations, delete dead ones, and reserve one account for production integrations.
blockers.title: 20 integrations per user account, hard cap

blockers.detail: 'The client secret is shown only when the integration is created.' The same one-time rule applies to Service App secrets and bot tokens; regenerating invalidates the old value immediately.
blockers.howToClear: Vault the secret and tokens at creation time; plan regeneration as a coordinated rotation.
blockers.title: Client secret is shown exactly once

blockers.detail: Scopes chosen at registration are fixed for the authorization request: you must 'request the same registered scopes during authorization'. Changing course means editing the integration and re-authorizing users, and Cisco steers everyone to minimum scopes (App Hub review enforces it).
blockers.howToClear: Finalize the minimal scope set before registering; treat scope additions as a re-authorization event.
blockers.title: Requested scopes must match the registered set

sources.label: Service Apps (admin authorization, App Hub submission, token lifetimes)

tested: Read-only verification: the three app types, integration creation and scope rules, token lifetimes, Service App admin authorization, and the App Hub review process were checked against current developer.webex.com pages (no app created, nothing submitted)
unverified: App Hub review duration and any submission cost (docs state neither; the 2-3 week figure is from a Cisco blog, not documentation).
Whether a customer org's admin can block or allowlist third-party integrations org-wide in Control Hub (the pages read cover this only for Service Apps).
Exact authorization-code lifetime ('short-lived' is all the Authentication page states).
Whether refresh tokens rotate on every use for integrations (docs say to store 'any replacement refresh token returned' without stating a policy).
Any per-org or per-app user caps for integrations (none stated).

alternatives: Bot (a machine identity with its own long-lived token; acts as itself, never on behalf of a user; in group spaces it only sees messages that @mention it)

Service App (a powerful machine account provisioned in the customer's org, authorized by its Full Admin in Control Hub; for unattended org-wide automation that should not depend on a user's lifecycle)
flavor.recommended: An Integration in the Webex Developer Portal (My Webex Apps)
flavor.why: Webex offers three OAuth-based app types. The Integration is 'an OAuth 2.0 client registered with Webex' that 'receives a temporary access token after a Webex user signs in and approves the requested scopes': the only type where each end user personally authorizes access to their own account.

humanMust: Create the Integration in the Developer Portal with your Webex account
Select the minimal scope set and add all redirect URIs
Copy and vault the Client Secret at creation (shown once)
For Service Apps: each customer's Full Admin authorizes in Control Hub
name: Webex
nuances: Token lifetimes are stated as 'typically 14 days for the access token and 90 days for the refresh token', but the Authentication page advises using the expiration values returned by the service rather than assuming a fixed lifetime.

An integration's token 'is limited by its scopes and by the permissions of the user who authorized it': if that user leaves the company or changes password, the integration breaks. That lifecycle fragility is exactly what Service Apps exist to avoid.

Admin/compliance scopes are heavy: spark-compliance:* scopes grant org-wide powers (reading/deleting messages in all spaces, audit events), and a Service App requesting them also requires the authorizing Full Admin to hold the Compliance Officer role, or authorization fails.
Service App scope budget: the combined scope string is limited to around 880 characters (an error message in the same doc says around 800), so scope selection is a real constraint.

App Hub submission traps: logo must be exactly 512x512; the listing contact must be a real person (generic support@ emails are rejected); the landing page must be public, unauthenticated, and on your own domain.
FedRAMP/Webex for Government diverges: App Hub is not supported there and several scopes are marked not for FedRAMP customers.
prerequisites: Your redirect URIs (register every one the app can use)

steps.detail: Developer Portal > My Webex Apps > Create a New App > Create an Integration. Enter the user-facing name, description, and icon; add every redirect URI the app can use; select only the minimum integration scopes required.
steps.title: Create an Integration

steps.detail: Save and copy the Client ID and Client Secret immediately: the secret is shown only when the integration is created. Never expose it in browser or mobile code.
steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Secret (once)

steps.detail: Redirect the user to webexapis.com/v1/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, space-separated scope (must match the registered set), and an unpredictable state. Webex shows a grant dialog and redirects back with a one-time, short-lived code.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST to webexapis.com/v1/access_token with grant_type=authorization_code, client ID/secret, code, and the same redirect URI. The response contains the access token, refresh token, and their expiration values. Call APIs with Authorization: Bearer; refresh with grant_type=refresh_token at the same endpoint, storing any replacement refresh token returned.
steps.title: Exchange the code; handle refresh

steps.detail: (Optional, discoverability only) Click Submit to Webex App Hub on the app's registration form. A ticket opens; review covers marketing materials first, then functionality/usability testing with demo accounts. Checks include production-readiness (no demo apps), minimal scopes, and trademark rules. No stated timeline.
steps.time: Submission ~30 min; review duration not stated
steps.title: (Optional) Submit to Webex App Hub

tagline: Three OAuth app types, one right default: the Integration, where each user authorizes their own account. No Cisco review to connect users; the ceilings are a 20-integration cap per account and a client secret you see exactly once.

time.active: ~10 min of portal work + ~1 hr of standard flow code
time.total: Same day for integrations; Service Apps add per-customer admin authorization of unstated duration
